title: Section fronts: section index pages and homePage.layout sections as standard front-end settings
description:
Phase 5 of the `homePage` epic, but independent of the home-page data: the generic section index pages and a home page of section blocks, as standard front-end settings. Generalises Shipped's `main(page)` section landing (`Shipped-web/web/hooks.py`, tabs + label + description + lead story + latest + older link), the default section listing page, TI's `_home` showcase bands and p.apyr.us's section descriptions.

## Goal
With settings only, every section that has a listing page gets an index page (page 1 of its listing) with a header (label, description), an optional lead Story, the latest N entries, an optional Reference grid for that section, and a link to the older pages; and a site can switch its generated home page to a home of section blocks, one block per listed section, each linking to the section's index page.

## Settings (`standard/config.py`)
- `SectionConfig.index: SectionIndexConfig | None` from `urls.sections.<name>.index`: `{"lead": true, "latest": 12, "references": "recent" | null, "referencesCount": 6, "source": "pages/<file>.md" | null}`. `latest` defaults to the section's `pageSize`; `lead` default true; `references` default null (needs `homePage`); `source` lets a site author the whole index page as a Markus file (the same renderer as `pages[].source`), in which case the other keys are ignored.
- `HomePageSettings.layout` and `.perSection` from `homePage`: `{"layout": "latest" | "sections", "perSection": 4, "homeLead": true, "homeSections": [names] | null}` (the same `homePage` key the References and Threads use; `perSection` default 4, Ryan 2026-10-31). `latest` is today's behaviour (`listings.homeCount`). `sections` lists blocks of `perSection` entries for each section in `urls.sections` order (or the given order), each with label, description and a "More <label>" link to `/{base}/`. A section with no entries is skipped unless `listEmpty`.
- Validation: `homePage.layout: sections` on an unsectioned site is an error; `index.references` without `homePage` is an error; `perSection` and `latest` whole numbers.

## Files to change
- `standard/projector.py` `_plan`: in the listings loop, when `view.page == 1` and the section has `index`, use a new `_section_index_builder(section, view, site, listed)` instead of `_listing_builder`; page id stays `listing:<section>` (so `DEPENDS_ON` keeps working) and the digest adds `[section.index fields, lead fingerprint, home-page digest if references]`. Home: when `homePage.layout == "sections"`, build `home` from `_home_sections_view(listed)` -> tuple of `(SectionConfig, entries[:perSection])`, digest `[fingerprints of all chosen, section links, perSection]`.
- `standard/page.py`: `StandardPage` gains `section_index: SectionIndexView | None` and `home_sections: tuple[HomeSectionBlock, ...]`.
- `standard/components.py`: `section_index_html(page)`, `home_sections_html(page)`, `section_tabs_html(sections, current)` (Shipped's `_landing_tabs_html` generalised; uses `section.base`, not `section.name`, which was a bug in Shipped's "More" row).
- `standard/projector.py` `_body_html`: render these kinds before falling back to the listing body; `hooks.main`/`page_body` still win when a site defines them (so Shipped and TI keep working unchanged until they opt in).
- `standard/markdown.py` `_markdown_for`: twins for both: headings per section, entries as a Markdown list with links, and the `references` line as `::include{kind="references" select=... count=... section=...}` so the twin matches the authored-page rule.
- `standard/assets/markus-components.css`: `markus-section-index`, `markus-home-sections`, `markus-section-block` (flat tones, rounded rectangles, no borders).
- `features_backend/section-fronts.feature` + steps; fixture `features_backend/fixtures/standard-site/sectioned/` gets a second projection.json variant (`sectioned-fronts/projection.json`) with `homePage.layout: sections` and `index` on `essays`; expected outputs under `expected/`.
- `docs/building-a-papyrus-static-site.md`: a "Section index pages and a home of sections" section with the settings.

## Gherkin scenarios (features_backend/section-fronts.feature)
- "A section with an index setting gets a front page with its description, a lead story and the latest entries, and page 2 keeps the plain listing"
- "A home of sections shows one block per section in configured order, each linking to the section index"
- "A section with no entries is skipped on the home of sections unless listEmpty"
- "A site that keeps homePage.layout latest renders exactly what it rendered before" (byte-equal against the existing `sectioned/expected/index.html`)
- "A section index that names a references selection shows that section's accepted References once, after the stories" (uses the home-page fixture)
- "A section index authored from a source file replaces the generated layout"
- "Publishing a story in one section rewrites that section's index and the home of sections, not another section's index"
- "Section index pages and the home of sections have Markdown twins and appear in llms.txt"
- "A site hook main() still wins over the generated section index" (Shipped unchanged)

## Acceptance checks
- behave + unit tests green; the sectioned fixture's existing expected files unchanged.
- Build p.apyr.us's `web/` locally with `homePage.layout: sections` added in a scratch copy (site repo read-only; do not commit) and eyeball `/index.html`, `/papyrus/index.html`. p.apyr.us adopting it is a separate site PR (merges freely per Ryan).

## Dependencies
Optional on: references include (only for `index.references`). Blocks: docs.
